items.stem: If a central bank raises interest rates to reduce inflation, what is the most likely short-term effect on aggregate demand?

options.text: Aggregate demand falls as borrowing and spending become more expensive
options.rationale: Correct: higher rates raise the cost of borrowing and saving's reward, tending to reduce consumption and investment.

options.text: Aggregate demand rises because saving becomes less attractive
options.rationale: Higher rates make saving more attractive, not less, reducing current spending.

options.text: Aggregate demand is unaffected by interest rates
options.rationale: Interest rates are a key channel through which monetary policy affects demand.

options.text: Aggregate demand rises because investment becomes cheaper
options.rationale: Higher rates make investment more expensive, not cheaper.

items.explanation: Correct: higher rates raise the cost of borrowing and saving's reward, tending to reduce consumption and investment.

items.stem: In a market, a decrease in the price of a good, other things equal, will normally cause:

options.text: An increase in the quantity demanded (a movement along the demand curve)
options.rationale: Correct: a price fall causes a movement along the demand curve, increasing quantity demanded.

options.text: A shift of the whole demand curve to the right
options.rationale: A price change moves along the curve; it does not shift the curve.
Lower price normally raises, not lowers, quantity demanded.
For a normal good, quantity demanded responds to price.

items.explanation: Correct: a price fall causes a movement along the demand curve, increasing quantity demanded.

items.stem: Select TWO functions performed by the financial system of an economy.

options.text: Channelling funds from savers to borrowers
options.rationale: Correct: intermediation moves funds from surplus to deficit units.

options.text: Providing a mechanism for payments and settlement
options.rationale: Correct: the financial system provides payment and settlement services.
Minimum wages are set by government/legislation, not the financial system.
Producing goods is the real economy, not the financial system.
This is a government administrative function, unrelated to the financial system.

items.explanation: Correct: intermediation moves funds from surplus to deficit units.
